text:
I need to tell our staff that we're ending fully remote work. I'm one of the three partners at an architecture firm with 46 architects and designers.

What I can say:
- From September 1, everyone works in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
- 15 of our people were hired as fully remote in 2021 and 2022. 4 of them live more than two hours from the office.
- Those 4 can keep working remotely until the end of next year. After that, they come in once a week.
- Last year we lost two large hospital projects in the final interview. Both clients told us our team seemed not to know each other.
- Based on our review records, junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project.
- The partners have been coming in one day a week. We'll be in all three days too.

Keep it to one page. It goes out by email before an all-staff meeting on Friday.

Before I draft, a few questions. Each answer would change what goes in the email:

1. **Which year does this start, and when does it end for the four?** It's November now. I'm reading this as office days from 1 September 2027, with the four long-distance people coming in once a week from January 2028. Is that right?
2. **What are you offering the other 11 people who were hired as fully remote?** For example, help with travel costs, a later start date, or a chance to talk to a partner one-on-one. These 11 were hired on remote terms and now have to come in three days a week. They will read the email looking for this first. If you have nothing for them yet, tell me, and I'll write around it honestly.
3. **What happens on Monday and Friday?** Can people work from home those days, or come in if they like? Is there anything else that stays flexible, such as hours?
4. **Can people ask for an exception, for example for caring duties or health reasons? If so, who do they go to?**
5. **Who signs it?** Should it come from all three partners by name or from you alone? And should it say the Friday meeting is for questions?

1. Yes, that's right. Office days from 1 September 2027, and the four come in once a week from January 2028.
2. We'll pay up to $150 a month toward commuting for anyone who lives more than 30 miles away. That applies to everyone, not just the 11. Nothing else for them beyond that.
3. I don't know. We haven't decided that.
4. No, I can't offer exceptions to anyone beyond those 4. Questions can go to me or to HR.
5. From me alone, Paul Whitaker. And yes, say the meeting is for questions. It's Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio. Questions before then can come to me or HR.

I've written the email from you, Paul. It's about 480 words, so it fits on one page.

<final_document>
**Subject: Office days from 1 September 2027**

Everyone,

From 1 September 2027, everyone at the firm will work in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. This ends fully remote work here. Before we meet on Friday, I want to explain why we're doing this and what it means for you.

**Why we're making this change**

Two things changed our minds.

Last year we lost two large hospital projects in the final interview. Both clients told us the same thing: our team seemed not to know each other. They weren't questioning anyone's skill. They were watching how we worked together in the room, and they didn't see people who were used to working side by side.

Our review records also show that junior staff hired since 2022 are taking about 30% longer to reach the point where they lead a project. That isn't their fault. A lot of what gets someone ready to lead comes from working near people who already do it. You overhear a client call, someone marks up your drawing at your desk, or you get pulled into a conversation. We haven't been giving our newer people enough of that.

The partners haven't helped. We've been coming in one day a week. From September, we will be in on all three days as well.

**What this means for you**

- **Office days:** Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, starting 1 September 2027.
- **Commuting support:** If you live more than 30 miles from the office, the firm will pay up to $150 a month toward your commuting costs. This applies to everyone, not only people hired as remote.
- **Colleagues who live more than two hours away:** You can keep working remotely until the end of 2027. From January 2028, you will come in one day a week.
- **Exceptions:** We are not able to make individual exceptions beyond the arrangement above.

We're telling you almost ten months ahead so you have time to plan.

**To those of you we hired as fully remote**

Fifteen of you joined us in 2021 and 2022 on fully remote terms. This changes what you agreed to when you joined, and I won't pretend it doesn't. For most of you it means coming in three days a week. Some of you will have hard choices to make about how this fits your life. If you want to talk it through, please come to me or to HR directly.

**Friday**

We'll meet on Friday at 10 a.m. in the main studio. The meeting is for your questions, so I'll keep my part short. If you'd rather ask something before then, or in private, come to me or to HR.

Paul Whitaker
Partner
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send it:

- **Mondays and Fridays:** I didn't mention them because you haven't decided yet. Expect this to be one of the first questions on Friday. Have an answer ready, or be ready to say when you'll decide.
- **The four long-distance staff:** If you haven't spoken to them yet, try to do it before the email goes out. Otherwise they'll find out about their arrangement at the same time as everyone else.
- **Employment terms:** The 15 people hired as fully remote may have that written into their contracts or offer letters. It's worth asking HR or your employment adviser whether changing those terms needs anything formal beyond this email.
